meta.name: Teo Tumbler
meta.logline: A ten-year-old lock-whisperer who can open any door in a city of living machines will only speak through his brass puppet — until the city's oldest Gate demands he say his own wish out loud, in front of everyone.

core.wound: At eight, frozen on stage at the Machine Day talent show, he let out one terrified hiccup — the Tin Chorus recorded it and the whole city used it as a doorbell chime for a year.
core.lie: If they really see me, they will laugh.
core.truth: Being seen is the price of being known.
core.central_paradox: The boy who can hear every secret a lock keeps won't let anyone hear one word of his own: the ear that makes him a genius at listening is the wall he hides behind.
core.dramatic_question: At the Grand Unlocking, will Teo speak his own wish to the Gate — or let his puppet answer for him and lose the apprenticeship?
core.spark_links: A boy terrified of being heard becomes a locksmith because locks are the only things that talk to him privately; in a city where machines are alive, the locks gossip and he 'tells fortunes' by repeating what they say — through a puppet, so it's never his voice; the keyhole-shaped birthmark the kids mocked is the visible echo of the work he hides in.

goals.want: Become the youngest apprentice of the Great Gate, the ancient talking lock that guards the city's clocktower.
goals.need: Let himself be seen and heard as he is — hiccups, birthmark and all.
goals.motivation: The Gate's apprentice is the most respected voice in the city; if the Gate chooses him, nobody can laugh at him again.
goals.arc_goal: Gain the confidence to be heard in his own voice
goals.goal_climax: At the Grand Unlocking, in front of the whole square and the Tin Chorus, the Gate will open only for an applicant who speaks their own name and a true wish aloud — not through a puppet.
goals.conflicting_goals: The apprenticeship he wants requires exactly the thing he has organised his whole life to avoid: standing in front of a crowd and talking in his own voice.
goals.scene_goal_example: Get the grumpy bakery door to admit who has been stealing croissants — without the baker noticing that it's Teo, not Clack, doing the talking.

methods.how: He presses his ear to any lock and hears its gossip — who came home late, who lost a key, who is in love. In the ads, every door he touches suddenly blurts out a funny secret.
He quietly lets locked-out neighbours back in at night and leaves a chalk smiley on the door, never his name.
Through Clack, his puppet, he is the funniest kid in the city — sharp impressions of every machine and adult; on his own he can barely say hello.

flaws.how_it_shows: With more than three people watching, his voice turns into hiccups; in ads this is the running gag — every big moment cuts to a hiccup.
Lets Clack do all the talking, including apologies and birthday wishes, and then believes people like Clack, not him.

identification.superpower: Lock-listening: he can open any lock in the city by hearing what it wants.
identification.vulnerability: Laughter: one giggle from an audience and his hands shake so badly he can't hold a pick.
identification.sympathy_hook: In the first spot he spends his pocket money on a new doorbell for the old widow whose door still plays his hiccup — so nobody has to hear it anymore.
identification.first_appearance: Night street: a little kid kneels at a sulking front door, presses his ear to it, nods — the door sighs and swings open; the grateful owner turns to thank him and finds only a chalk smiley.
identification.jeopardy: If the Tin Chorus catches his voice again, the whole city will hear it — and the festival will be broadcast live.

states.passive: Spends evenings in the workshop under his grandmother's counter, oiling locks and talking to them in a whisper.
states.reactive: The Gate announces it will choose an apprentice at the Grand Unlocking — the first chance in fifty years.
states.active: Trains every night to say one sentence without hiccuping: to locks first, then to pigeons, then to the bakery queue.

psychology.emotional_baseline: Bright and curious in private, shrinking and silent in public.
inner_monologue: Don't hiccup. Don't hiccup. Don't hiccup.
Clack can say it. Clack is funnier anyway.
psychology.interprets_experience: When a plan goes wrong, it's because he was noticed; when it goes right, it's Clack's credit.
psychology.psychological_issues: Severe stage fright with hiccuping attacks; compulsively checks reflective surfaces to see if the birthmark is showing.
psychology.insecurity: That the real Teo, without the puppet, is boring and ridiculous.
psychology.strong_beliefs: Every door has a reason to stay shut, and you open it by listening, not by forcing.
psychology.strongest_trigger: The doorbell chime made from his hiccup.
psychology.childhood: Raised by his grandmother, a locksmith who talks to everyone; his parents run a famous machine-theatre and are always on tour, so applause belongs to them, not to him.
psychology.visual_device: Whenever Teo speaks through Clack, the ad's sound is crisp; when he tries his own voice, the soundtrack drops to his heartbeat and a single ticking lock until he finishes the sentence.

description.name_meaning: Teo, short for Teodor, 'gift of god' — he's a gift he won't unwrap; a tumbler is the tiny pin inside a lock that has to line up before it opens, and also a clown who falls on stage.
description.cultural_background: Grew up in the Brassworks quarter, where families pass down a craft and a nickname; dinner-table talk is half human, half machine slang ('don't jam', 'oil your manners').

physical.height_build: Small for his age, round-cheeked and soft, with long arms that seem borrowed from an older kid.
physical.face: Warm light-brown skin, big brown eyes that look down first, a gap between his front teeth, and a keyhole-shaped birthmark on his left cheek.
physical.hair: Thick copper-red curls that never lie flat, longer on the left so he can hide the birthmark behind them.
physical.first_impression: A small, curious kid hiding inside a too-big raincoat, listening harder than anyone in the room.

life_events.event: Opened his grandmother's stuck safe by listening to it while the adults argued over a crowbar.
life_events.effect: Discovered that locks would talk to him — and that he could be useful without saying a word.

life_events.event: Froze at the Machine Day talent show; his hiccup became the city's doorbell chime for a year.
life_events.effect: Learned the lie that being heard means being laughed at.

life_events.event: Built Clack, a talking brass lock-puppet, and discovered everyone laughed WITH Clack.
life_events.effect: Started living entirely through the puppet and believing nobody would like him without it.

hobbies: Collecting old keys with no locks
Doing impressions of machines through Clack
Racing wind-up mice along the tramlines

speech.manner: In his own voice: whispered half-sentences, lots of 'um'; through Clack: fast, sharp, loud, with machine sound effects.
sample_lines: (as Clack) Madam, your door says you snore. I'm just the messenger.
(own voice) Um. It's... it's open now.
It's what the lock said, not me!

sociology.status: A well-liked neighbourhood oddball; adults trust him with their keys, kids still call him 'Hiccup'.
sociology.education: Third grade at the Brassworks school; secretly reads his grandmother's locksmith manuals at night.
sociology.money: Earns tips in sweets and coins; saves them in a jar shaped like a padlock.
sociology.friends_family: Grandmother Ida, loud and loving; parents always away on tour; one human friend, Mina, who never laughs at the hiccups.
sociology.place: The Brassworks quarter, a street of workshops where doors, lamps and trams are alive and opinionated.
sociology.world_events: The Great Gate falls silent for the first time in fifty years and announces the Grand Unlocking; every family in the city wants their child to be chosen.

description.biggest_disappointment: His parents watched the talent-show clip on tour and laughed too — kindly, but they laughed.
description.most_valued: His grandmother's workshop, where nobody expects him to perform.
description.secret_dream: To stand on the clocktower balcony and give a speech the whole city listens to — in his own voice; he imagines himself older, the Gate's keeper, with Clack retired on a shelf.
description.missing: One moment of being applauded for himself, not for Clack or for his parents' name.

fears.root: The talent-show hiccup that became the city's doorbell.

fears.fear: Nobody would like him without Clack
fears.root: Since he built the puppet, people only ever laughed with it, never with him.

fears.mask: Clack — loud, cheeky and fearless, everything Teo isn't.
fears.courage_source: Mina, who once told him the hiccup was the best part of the whole show.
fears.overcoming: Takes one small step at a time: says one sentence to a lock, then to a pigeon, then to the bakery queue — and finally to the Gate.

uniqueness.twist: A fortune teller who doesn't predict anything — he just repeats what doors overhear, and refuses to tell his own.
quirks: Knocks twice before touching any lock, as a greeting
Hides the birthmark behind a curl whenever he passes a shop window
Holds his breath and counts tumblers when nervous, which makes the hiccups worse
Keeps every key he's ever found on a ring that jingles when he runs
Says 'sorry' to doors he has to force

lifestyle.tastes: Loves the clicking songs of the tram depot and silent comedy films where nobody talks.
lifestyle.shopping: The flea market of broken machines, paying in fixed locks.
lifestyle.food: Only eats sandwiches cut into triangles, because 'squares jam'.
lifestyle.vehicle: A squeaky scooter he repaired himself, with a bell he removed.
lifestyle.love_style: Fixes things for the people he loves instead of saying it.
lifestyle.nonverbal_tics: Pulls his raincoat hood over his head when people look at him; rubs his left cheek.
lifestyle.spirituality: Believes every lock has a little soul and leaves them a drop of oil 'for good luck'.

uniqueness.stress_relief: Takes apart an old padlock and puts it back together, over and over.
uniqueness.dream_vacation: A quiet island with only one door, and it's always open.

backstory.biography: Teo was born in the Brassworks quarter to two famous machine-theatre performers who were almost always on tour, so he grew up in his grandmother Ida's locksmith workshop. At five he opened her jammed safe just by listening to it, and discovered that the city's living locks would talk to him in whispers. At eight his parents insisted he perform at the Machine Day talent show; he froze, hiccuped once, and the Tin Chorus — the city's robot choir that records every sound it likes — turned the hiccup into a doorbell chime that rang all over the city for a year. Kids started calling him 'Hiccup' and noticed the keyhole-shaped birthmark on his cheek. At nine he built Clack, a brass lock-puppet, and found that everyone laughed with Clack, never at him. Now ten, he opens doors for neighbours at night, 'tells fortunes' by repeating what locks overhear, and speaks only through Clack — just as the Great Gate announces it will choose an apprentice.

world.who_rules: The Council of Clocks, old machines who decide the city's schedule, and the Great Gate, whose word is final.
world.boundaries: The city wall of sleeping doors: nobody has passed it since the Gate fell silent; beyond it is the Rusted Field, where machines that stopped talking are taken.
world.hierarchy: Ancient machines, then famous performers, then craftspeople, then everyone else; children are listened to last.
world.good_and_bad: Good is keeping your word and oiling what you love; bad is breaking a lock instead of listening to it.
world.worth_dying_for: Nothing — this is a comedy; worth losing face for: a friend.
world.worth_living_for: The Grand Unlocking festival, when every door in the city opens at once.
world.best_and_worst: Best: the Gate speaks again. Worst: the city's doors all lock themselves forever.
world.survival_vs_comfort: Comfort — this city's biggest worries are reputation and who gets the best festival seat.

backstory.connection_to_past: His hiccup is literally part of the city's sound; the Tin Chorus still plays it at festivals.
backstory.distance_from_peers: Other Brassworks kids perform at every festival; Teo is the only one who works instead.
backstory.daily_life: School by day, workshop after dinner, rounds of locked-out neighbours at night; eats triangle sandwiches on the workshop step.
backstory.decision_style: Presses his ear to the nearest door and 'asks' it; under pressure he hands the decision to Clack.
key_locations: Grandmother Ida's workshop: a cave of keys hanging from the ceiling like wind chimes
The Brassworks street, where every door has an opinion about you
The clocktower square and the Great Gate, with its keyhole as tall as a house

contradictions.behavior: Relaxed and chatty in the workshop — the only adult he talks to in his own voice.
Bossy and brave when she's in trouble; he'll talk in his own voice for her and not even notice.

contradictions.with_whom: Rook, the talent-show champion who mocks him
contradictions.behavior: Silent, hidden behind Clack's insults — he wins every argument and still feels like he lost.

traits.energy: Low in public, high in the workshop
traits.temperament: Melancholic with sanguine bursts through Clack
habits: Counts lock tumblers under his breath
Checks his reflection for the birthmark
traits.best_trait: Talented: nobody in the city can open a lock — or do an impression — like Teo.
traits.worst_trait: Fake: he hides behind Clack's voice until even he forgets what his own sounds like.

reactions.reaction: Pulls up his hood and lets Clack crack a joke first.
Sits down and listens to it for as long as it takes.
Forgets the hiccups and speaks loudly in his own voice.

others_say: That boy could open a bank vault, but ask him his name and he turns into a teapot.
Clack is hilarious. Teo? Teo is the quiet one holding Clack.

destiny.ordinary_world: Workshop, night rounds and fortune-telling through Clack in the Brassworks quarter.
destiny.void: Nobody has ever heard the real Teo, including Teo.
destiny.threshold: The Great Gate announces the Grand Unlocking — and the rule that applicants must speak in their own voice.
destiny.ordeal: On the festival stage the Tin Chorus plays his hiccup chime to the whole square; Rook laughs, and Clack's jaw jams.
destiny.transformation: With Clack jammed, Teo speaks his own name and wish — hiccups and all; the square goes quiet, then the Gate laughs with him, not at him.
destiny.ending: The Gate opens and chooses him; the city keeps the hiccup chime, now as the sound of the Gate opening. Clack gets a quiet seat on the workshop shelf.

look.shape_language: Round and soft everywhere — cheeks, curls, raincoat hood, sneaker toes — with one hard, angular shape: Clack, the brass puppet on his shoulder, all sharp corners and teeth.
look.silhouette: A small figure inside a too-big raincoat with the hood half up, a tuft of curls sticking out, and a boxy little puppet on one shoulder. It avoids the stock 'cute kid inventor' look of goggles and a jumpsuit.
look.perfection: Clean and cared for by his grandmother, but always slightly too big for his clothes; tools spotless, sleeves rolled four times.

signature_item.item: Clack, a brass lock-puppet with a keyhole mouth and two rivet eyes
signature_item.story: Built at nine from a broken padlock; it speaks for him since the talent-show disaster.
signature_item.how_carried: Sits on his left shoulder, held by a leather strap; in the ending it rests on the workshop shelf.

marks.location: Left cheek, usually under a curl
marks.origin: Born with it; the talent-show kids made it famous.
Five years of working in his grandmother's workshop.

movement.gait: Quick, light, slightly hunched steps, always close to walls and doors.
movement.idle_pose: Head tilted to the left as if listening to a door, hands in the raincoat pockets.
movement.signature_gesture: Two soft knocks with one knuckle before touching any lock.
movement.under_stress: Shoulders up to his ears, hood up, hand drifts to cover his left cheek; then a hiccup.

outfit.why: Hand-me-down from his parents' theatre merch.

outfit.piece: Mustard-yellow raincoat, two sizes too big, sleeves rolled
outfit.why: Grandma bought it to 'grow into'; the hood is his favourite hiding place.

outfit.piece: Teal shorts with a leather tool belt of tiny picks and a key ring
Red canvas sneakers with mismatched laces
outfit.why: He replaced one lace with lock wire after it snapped.

palette.name: Raincoat Mustard
palette.meaning: His hiding place and his warmth — the brightest thing on him, which he hates.

palette.name: Copper Curl
palette.meaning: His family, the Brassworks, and the curl that hides the birthmark.

palette.name: Workshop Teal
palette.meaning: Grandma's workshop, where he is safe.

palette.name: Sneaker Red
palette.meaning: The courage he hasn't used yet.

props: Ring of keys with no locks
Oil can the size of a thumb
story_reads: He's hiding: hood half up, curl over the cheek, standing close to a door.
He's good with his hands: a neat tool belt and tiny picks on a kid.
He has a louder friend than himself: the brass puppet on his shoulder looks braver than he does.
look.art_style: Stylized 3D animated-film look, soft rounded forms, warm colourful lighting
look.turnaround_notes: Clack sits on his LEFT shoulder in every view; birthmark on the LEFT cheek, hidden by a longer curl on the left; raincoat hood half up; tool belt on the hips.

body.why: A small ten-year-old with long arms 'borrowed from an older kid'; he hunches to hide and tilts his head to the left, the ear he listens to locks with.

accessories.item: Clack, a small brass lock-puppet with a keyhole mouth
leather tool belt with tiny lock picks and a key ring
